name: Vegetables in Black Bean Sauce
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice. Put it in a lidded saucepan with 420 ml of the measured water, bring to a boil, cover and cook over the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes before fluffing. Cut broccoli into small florets, pepper and onion into bite-size pieces, baby corn in halves, mushrooms into slices, and trim the snow peas.

Rinse the fermented black soybeans briefly and drain; roughly chop half so their flavor spreads while the other half remain visible. These are salty fermented Chinese soybeans, not ordinary cooked black beans or Korean chunjang paste. Mince garlic and ginger. Whisk the remaining 250 ml water, soy sauce, rice vinegar, cornstarch and sugar until smooth.

Heat 25 ml oil in a wide wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry broccoli and baby corn for 3 minutes, then add onion, mushrooms and bell pepper for 2 minutes. Add snow peas and stir-fry another 1 minute. Move the vegetables to a plate while still bright and slightly crisp so they do not overcook in the sauce.

Add the remaining 15 ml oil to the hot wok. Stir garlic, ginger and the chopped and whole fermented black beans for 30–45 seconds until fragrant without burning. Stir the prepared liquid again to lift the settled starch, pour it in and simmer for 1–2 minutes until glossy and lightly thickened. Taste before adding any salt; the beans and soy sauce are already salty.

Return all vegetables to the wok and toss for 1 minute until hot and evenly coated, with distinct black-bean flecks still visible. Divide the stir-fry among four bowls and serve with the fluffy jasmine rice separately, as in the photograph.
tips: Use fermented Chinese black soybeans (douchi), not canned black kidney beans and not Korean black-bean noodle paste. Rinsing moderates their saltiness. The vegetables should stay crisp-tender and the sauce glossy rather than becoming a thick black puree.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
